blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: The rollback path after finalize contradicts the restore semantics in Control plane and GitOps and understates the outage. Restore runs from the host CLI into an empty deployment. It needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, which opens a higher `storeEpoch`, and it invalidates sessions and API tokens. Without an operator-supplied revocation list, no Node certificate issued before the restore is admitted until its Node re-enrolls, and until then those Nodes serve detached. That means every Node of every Cluster, not only the Nodes enrolled since the backup. An operator who plans from this sentence expects a partial re-enrollment and gets a fleet-wide detached state.
blocking.evidence: Ruralz Control upgrades, step 4: "After it, rollback means `ruralz control restore` from the first backup, losing every later Control Store write (Rollouts, audit entries, Enrollments); Nodes enrolled since re-enroll." Control plane and GitOps, Backup, restore and `postgres`: "`ruralz control restore` runs only from the host CLI into an empty deployment. Before any delivery it needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, opening a higher `storeEpoch` ... without one, no Node certificate issued before the restore is admitted ... until its Node re-enrolls or the list arrives. Those Nodes serve detached."
blocking.fix: Rewrite step 4 to match Control plane and GitOps. After finalize, rollback means restoring the pre-upgrade backup with N-1 binaries into an empty deployment. That opens a higher `storeEpoch`, rotates the online key, invalidates sessions and API tokens, and needs the operator's revocation list. Without the list, every Node serves detached until it re-enrolls. Link to Control plane and GitOps, Backup, restore and postgres, and give this cost as the reason for the soak before finalize.

blocking.issue: The Node upgrade handover surface names `assignmentIndex`, a persisted field that no document defines. The row also misses the state that really crosses versions. Control plane and GitOps persists the fence pair (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`), `promotionSeq` and the anchor-set `version` under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/`. Suppose an N binary changes that file's encoding and a rolled-back N-1 binary reads it: the N-1 Node then sends a transient NACK for every assignment, or accepts a stale one. That cross-version case is the one this row exists to govern, and it is not covered.
blocking.evidence: "| Node upgrade handover | `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` file lock, candidate, persisted `assignmentIndex`, Unix-socket readiness message | A release MUST hand over from, and roll back to, every line in support ..." versus Control plane and GitOps, Fencing stale replicas: "Nodes persist the highest pair activated under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/`, compare pairs in order and send a transient NACK for a lower one".
blocking.fix: Replace `assignmentIndex` with the persisted (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`) pair, `promotionSeq` and the anchor-set `version`. List `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/` (`node.id`, certificate, key, fence values) beside `lkg/` as part of the surface, and add Control plane and GitOps as an owner. Keep the rule that format changes are additive, or carry a version marker that the older side handles safely.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: Neither State Store migration path preserves consumptive state. Two-step path: when N Nodes switch to the new layout, the new Quota and Token Budget keys start empty. A monthly allowance is then admitted again for the rest of its window, so admission reaches 2x for the whole window, not just for the signal's propagation time. GCRA state also resets and allows an extra burst per key. Shared-hash-tag path: a Cluster may stay mixed N and N-1 indefinitely ('Any mix of N and N-1, at any time'). While it does, N-1 Nodes keep writing only the old key, so if the N script updates only the new key, the counters split. Both paths break the full-reservation admission rule of P8 and pack 8.9.
blocking.evidence: "A key layout or script change either keeps the replaced key's hash tag, so one script covers both keys, or switches in two steps: N Nodes read and write the N-1 layout until the Cluster's minimum Node version reaches N ... During a switch, split consumptive counters (GCRA, Quotas, Token Budgets) may admit up to 2x a global limit for the signal's propagation time (hypothesis)"; skew table: "| Nodes within one Cluster | Any mix of N and N-1, at any time |".
blocking.fix: Require consumptive state to use only the shared-hash-tag path. While any N-1 Node may serve, the N script reads and writes both the old and the new key atomically in one EVAL, still one round trip. After the minimum Node version reaches N, it migrates lazily: read the old key, write the new key and delete the old one. Allow a two-step switch only for non-consumptive state such as caches, or only at a window boundary. State the bound per state class, for example 'no over-admission for Quotas and Token Budgets; at most one extra burst per key for GCRA (hypothesis)', and hand the bound to Scalability and distributed state.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: The MUST that a release can roll back to every supported line cannot hold once Bundles use fields added in N, and the document never names that point. After Figure 2 node k, the active Revision and Last-Known-Good contain fields that N-1 does not serve. An in-place rollback then fails safely, because the N-1 process cannot compile the holder's Revision and the N process keeps serving. A restart-based rollback has no predecessor process: examples are a Kubernetes image rollback or a systemd restart with the old binary. The Node boots Last-Known-Good and gets RZ-CFG-024. It then receives the same assigned Revision, NACKs and stays not ready; in file mode both the Bundle and Last-Known-Good fail. A fleet-wide binary rollback, the usual response to an N regression, therefore takes Nodes out of service. That contradicts both the rollback MUST and the claim that skew never costs an active Revision.
blocking.evidence: Versioned surfaces: "A release MUST hand over from, and roll back to, every line in support"; skew table: "| Last-Known-Good and Node | ... | Newer field, booted by N-1 | RZ-CFG-024; the Node waits for the Control Stream or stays not ready (pack 8.2) |"; Figure 2 node k: "Oldest Node schema level rises; Bundles may use new fields".
blocking.fix: Qualify the rollback MUST: a Node binary rolls back to N-1 only while its active Revision and Last-Known-Good use no field above N-1's schema levels. Mark Figure 2 node k as the point after which a binary rollback first needs a Rollout, or a file-mode Revision, without N-only fields. Have Ruralz Control flag Clusters whose active Revision uses N-only fields, and recommend a soak before Bundles adopt new fields. Name Zero-downtime upgrades and hot reload as the owner of the procedure.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: Before finalize, the Raft rules keep only replicated traffic readable by N-1. Local persisted state is not covered: bbolt records, local Raft snapshots, content objects and audit segments on each replica's disk. An N replica could therefore write a local format that N-1 cannot read, and the promised 'normal rolling step' back to N-1 would fail at startup. After finalize, nothing stops an N-1 binary that starts against the finalized log. Unless it is required to halt, it skips or misapplies the version-advance entry and the N-only entries, and its FSM silently diverges. The skew table lists this case as out of policy, but its Enforcement cell only links to a section that states no enforcement.
blocking.evidence: Ruralz Control upgrades, step 2: "While the cluster version is N-1, every replica writes only N-1 encodings in log entries, snapshots sent to followers and the write-forwarding and status-forwarding classes on 8092"; step 4: "Before finalize, returning any replica to N-1 is a normal rolling step."; skew row: "| Ruralz Control replicas | ... | N-2; an N-1 binary after finalize | [Ruralz Control upgrades](#ruralz-control-upgrades) |".
blocking.fix: Widen rule 2 to all persisted replica state: local Raft snapshots, bbolt records, content objects and audit segments stay readable by N-1 until finalize. Add a rule that a replica stops before serving, and exports a metric, when its FSM meets a cluster version above its binary's or an unknown entry type; it never skips the entry. The same check runs at startup against the latest snapshot and log, so an N-1 binary cannot join a finalized cluster.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: The rule that N decodes only N-1 encodings does not survive hashicorp/raft log retention or the immutable content store. First, raft snapshots only after a threshold of new entries and keeps trailing logs after each snapshot. In a low-write Control Store, the newest snapshot and the logs replayed at restart, or sent to a lagging or joining follower, can therefore still hold N-2 or older encodings when a replica starts on N. Finalize forces no snapshot or compaction. Second, Revision content, diffs, plans and sealed audit segments are digest-addressed and immutable, so they cannot be re-encoded at finalize and keep their original format for their whole retention. An N binary that reads only N-1 encodings then fails at startup, during follower catch-up, or when reading old audit segments and Revisions for rollback.
blocking.evidence: Upgrade order: "Ruralz Control upgrades one minor at a time, since N decodes only N-1 encodings"; step 2: "N binaries MUST decode every N-1 log entry, record and snapshot."; Control plane and GitOps, Control Store table: "| Revision content, diffs, plans, sealed audit segments | Content store, on a quorum before the referencing entry | Yes |".
blocking.fix: Split the rule by data class. For mutable Raft state: after the version-advance entry commits, every replica takes a user snapshot past that index and truncates its trailing logs, and it reports completion to the leader. The next upgrade is refused until every voter has reported, so no older encoding survives. For immutable content objects: each object carries a format marker, and every release decodes every content and audit-segment format still inside the retention window. Remove a decoder only after a documented rewrite or expiry, and add this to the Versioned surfaces table.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: Rendering has no cluster-version gate, so during a mixed-replica upgrade a Revision depends on which replica leads. With N and N-1 replicas, an N leader materializes N's `ruralz/v1alpha1` defaults and an N-1 leader materializes N-1's defaults. The same commit then renders to different digests. CI renders stop matching Ruralz Control. A promotion can also carry into prod a default that staging never ran, because pack 8.1 promotes a commit, not a digest, and each Environment renders its own Revision. That contradicts the claim that an election mid-upgrade is harmless, and the new default reaches Nodes before finalize.
blocking.evidence: Step 2: "... whichever replica leads, so an election mid-upgrade is harmless."; skew row: "| `ruralz bundle push` to Ruralz Control | CLI at N; N-1 only if N's release notes list no `ruralz/v1alpha1` default change |"; pack 8.1: "Promotion | Moves a source commit, not a digest".
blocking.fix: Until finalize, every replica renders at the cluster version's schema levels and defaults. An N binary can do this because every v1alpha1 default change is a new schema level. The version advance never re-renders recorded Revisions. State that the first Revision rendered after finalize under a changed default shows the change in its diff, and name the Configuration model as the owner of level-pinned rendering.

blocking.issue: The claim of one maintenance window every 6 months conflicts with the upgrade procedure. Each Ruralz Control step needs every voter at N, a 24-hour soak (target), and a finalize before the Nodes upgrade. The next Ruralz Control step then needs every Node at the new version (Figure 2 node b). Catching up two minors therefore takes at least two soaks and two Node passes in sequence, more than 48 hours, so an operator who plans one window from this sentence under-budgets the upgrade.
blocking.evidence: "An operator can plan one maintenance window every 6 months (target) and stay supported; it contains two single-minor steps, each upgrading Ruralz Control and then the Nodes." versus step 3: "Once every voter reports N and a 24-hour soak (target) has passed, an operator finalizes" and Figure 2 edges "i --> h", "h --> m", "m --> j".
blocking.fix: Say that the 6-monthly upgrade spans at least two soaks, about 2 to 3 days (target), in two single-minor steps. Alternatively, let Node upgrades start once every voter reports N, in parallel with the soak, since N replicas already serve N-1 Nodes. In that case redraw Figure 2 so that j follows g, and keep m for new record types only.

blocking.issue: The within-v1 rules allow removing a field with `reserved` but never tie the removal to the skew window. Suppose Ruralz Control N stops sending a field that an N-1 Node still reads, such as a promotion or signature field. The wire format stays compatible and `buf breaking` passes, yet the Node silently treats the field as unset. The document constrains only additions ('MUST NOT depend on an older Node understanding later additions'), so removal can break an in-policy Node.
blocking.evidence: "| Removed field | Only by `reserved` | No |"; "Ruralz Control upgrades first and MUST NOT depend on an older Node understanding later additions."
blocking.fix: Allow removal only after the field has been deprecated, and neither read nor required by any in-policy version, for at least 2 minor releases (target). Until then the sender keeps populating it. State the same rule for fields a Node sends to Ruralz Control, and have the `buf breaking` job run against the last tag of every line still inside the skew window.

non_blocking.suggestion: `Hello` already carries an anchor-set `version` field, so 'Only `EnrollRequest` carries `version`' is imprecise and option (a) of OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-4 is ambiguous. Name the proposed field distinctly, for example `binaryVersion`, in the text and in the Open question.

Rule 2 relies on an RZ-CFG-028 NACK that Ruralz Control cannot reproduce, so it is treated as transient and retried. A missing import never succeeds on retry. Consider letting the Node mark it with NACK `class` so that Ruralz Control pauses instead of quarantining, and record the gap in OQ-wasm-plugin-system-13.

non_blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
non_blocking.suggestion: The regional Ruralz Control relay, Planned (M4), dials 8092 with role `relay` and has no skew row. State its allowed skew toward the replicas and the Nodes, and require relays to upgrade after the replicas and before the Nodes.

non_blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
non_blocking.suggestion: The CLI and REST API row cites RZ-CFG-006, a Bundle parse code, for an unknown REST API field. REST API errors belong to the `RZ-CP` registry (pack 8.6), so cite or request a CP code.

non_blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
non_blocking.suggestion: The skew section defines N as Ruralz Control's minor, while Release cadence and support windows uses N for the newest release. Use distinct symbols or say so explicitly, because a user whose Nodes sit on a supported N-2 line cannot run the newest Ruralz Control.

A render-changing bug fix in a patch breaks digest reproduction between the CLI and Ruralz Control, although the section says 'patches never matter'. State that render-changing fixes follow the default-change rule: minor only, a golden-corpus entry, and a release-note listing.

`pkg/` sits in the root module, which is tagged with the product version. A product 2.0.0 tag without a `/v2` module path is rejected by `go get` and `go install` for a module that has a `go.mod`, so any product major forces an import-path change across the monorepo. Say so, or move `pkg/` into its own module with its own tags, as done for `sdk/go`.
GHCR does not enforce immutable tags. Describe `X.Y.Z` as 'never re-pushed (policy)' and recommend pinning by digest.

With CRDs served through Ruralz Control's conversion webhook, the Kubernetes API cannot serve non-storage versions while Ruralz Control is down. Note this availability dependency, and the cluster-scoped RBAC on `customresourcedefinitions/status`, for Deployment topologies.

'Security fixes for every supported line' overstates the severity table, where Medium reaches N and N-1 and Low reaches N only. Say 'critical and high fixes for every supported line'. The body is about 3,900 of 4,000 words, so trim prose while applying the blocking fixes.

Consider adding the Node binary version, sent in `Hello` per OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-4.
